body.objective: Students will be able to research a work's style and history.
body.iCan: I can research a work's style and history.
successCriteria: I can research a work's composer, period and style
I can apply correct articulation, tone and feel for the style
I can write a programme note that informs an audience
body.hook: A Bach chorale, a Sousa march and a Duke Ellington chart can all be played by the same band, but if you play them all the same way, you'll get all three wrong. Stylistic accuracy starts with knowing where a piece comes from.

study.title: Know the Piece
study.question: How does research help an ensemble play in the right style?
study.passage:
Part 1, Research (20 minutes): For one piece in your concert folder, find: composer and dates; when and why it was written; the period or genre; key features of that style; one recording by a respected ensemble.
Part 2, Style sheet (15 minutes): Make a style sheet. Examples:
• March (Sousa, early 1900s): notes slightly separated, crisp accents, steady tempo, dynamics change at the trio (often softer first time), bold low brass.
• Chorale (Bach or band chorale): legato, connected air, balance toward the bass, breathe together at phrase ends.
• Big band swing (Ellington, Basie): swing eighths, short "dot" quarters, accents on off-beats, falls and doits, sections play as one.
• Contemporary concert band (for example Eric Whitacre or Kelly-Marie Murphy): extended techniques, clusters, attention to colour and space.
Part 3, Apply (15 minutes): Rehearse 16 bars using the style sheet. Record before and after.
Part 4, Programme note (10 minutes): Write 100 to 150 words for the concert program: who, when, why, what to listen for. No spoilers that would bore the audience; give them something to notice.

examples.title: March articulation
examples.problem: How are quarter notes played in a Sousa march?
examples.answer: Slightly separated and crisp with steady tempo
examples.explore: How would they differ in a chorale?

examples.title: Jazz quarter notes
examples.problem: How are quarter notes often played in big band swing?
examples.answer: Short and punchy ("dot") unless marked long

examples.title: Programme note
examples.problem: Write a programme note opening for a march.
examples.answer: "John Philip Sousa, 'The March King,' wrote this march in 1896; listen for the quiet trio melody that returns in full brass"
examples.explore: What else might the audience want to know?

examples.title: Chorale
examples.problem: What is the key to chorale style?
examples.answer: Connected air, balance from the bass up and breathing together

practice.a: The characteristic way music of a period or genre is played.
How notes are started and connected.
A short text about a piece in a concert program.

practice.q: Name two features of march style.
practice.a: Separated crisp notes, strong accents, steady tempo.

practice.q: Name two features of big band swing style.
practice.a: Swing eighths, short quarters, off-beat accents, section unity.

practice.q: Why listen to a professional recording?
practice.a: To hear accurate style and sound.

practice.q: What should a programme note include?
practice.a: Composer, when and why it was written, what to listen for.

practice.q: How should a chorale be played?
practice.a: Legato, balanced from the bass, breathing together.

practice.q: What is the trio in a march?
practice.a: A contrasting section, often softer and in a new key.

practice.q: How can the same rhythm be played differently in two styles?
practice.a: Articulation, length and accent change by style.

practice.q: Why is stylistic accuracy a form of respect?
practice.a: It honours the composer's intentions and the music's culture.

practice.q: How can a programme note improve the audience's listening?
practice.a: It gives them something specific to notice.

practice.q: How would you research a contemporary piece with few sources?
practice.a: Composer's website, interviews, score notes and premiere recordings.

misconceptions: Playing every piece with the same articulation
Thinking style is only about tempo
Writing programme notes that only list facts
